## General information

**Machine Generated Text (MGT) detection** analyses text to determine whether it was written by a human or generated by a large language model (LLM) such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, or similar AI systems. AI-generated text is increasingly used to produce disinformation at scale, fabricate quotes, or generate synthetic news articles.

## How to use it

Paste the text you want to analyse into the input field. The tool will return a score indicating the likelihood that the text was AI-generated, along with highlighted passages that show the most suspicious segments.

## How it works

The tool uses statistical and neural network-based classifiers trained on datasets of human-written and AI-generated text. It analyses stylistic patterns, perplexity, burstiness, and other linguistic features to distinguish human from machine authorship.

## Important notes

- No detection tool is 100% accurate. AI-generated text that has been heavily edited by a human may not be detected.
- The tool is most reliable on longer passages (several paragraphs). Short texts produce less reliable results.
- A high AI-probability score does **not** constitute proof of automated generation. Always combine with editorial judgment.

## Use cases

- Screening press releases, social media posts, or news articles for potential AI authorship
- Investigating suspected AI-driven disinformation campaigns
- Supporting research into the spread of AI-generated content
